quarterly_data.signal: Second-quarter revenue was approximately $33,000 versus $26,000 a year earlier, with approximately $100,000 of deferred revenue to be recognized on milestones under an existing joint development agreement. Net loss was $6.6 million ($0.04 per share) versus approximately $5 million; R&D expense approximately $3.9 million (from $2.6 million) and G&A approximately $3.4 million (from $2.3 million). Cash, equivalents and marketable securities were $95.9 million with no debt; cash used in operations was approximately $9.9 million and capex approximately $1.5 million in the first six months.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue approximately $33,000 (vs $26,000); net loss $6.6 million; R&D $3.9 million; cash $95.9 million

quarterly_data.signal: Customers: a new unnamed Fortune Global 500 customer moved into Stage 3 of the design-win process, bringing Stage 3 programs to five. The new program is initially focused on scale-across transceivers using coherent modulation; CEO said scale-across is making a strong comeback as operators connect campuses miles to tens of miles apart into one virtual data center using ultra-high-speed optical links, DWDM and coherent modulation. The Stage 3 job now is to meet the technical milestones for qualification and Stage 4. CFO: the Stage 1 and 2 pipeline remains strong; foundry wafer-run results will raise the confidence of target customers tied to specific foundries.

Foundry programs: three dedicated foundry runs are underway; two sets of wafers are expected in August and the third foundry's wafers in the fourth quarter, and a dedicated run with a fourth foundry is being prepared toward a tape-out later this year. The active foundry ecosystem now includes GlobalFoundries, Tower Semiconductor, SilTerra and a fourth unnamed partner. After wafer receipt Lightwave deposits and encapsulates the polymer, then tests and characterizes devices with customers; the runs are also used with the foundries to tune the process, yield and performance of high-bandwidth slot modulators. CEO expects the fourth quarter to give a much clearer technical picture.
quarterly_data.figure: three foundry runs underway; two wafer sets expected in August, third in the fourth quarter; fourth foundry tape-out later this year

quarterly_data.signal: Commercial agreements: one material supply and licensing agreement is already in place, and Lightwave is actively negotiating a new agreement with the customer whose program is the most advanced toward productization, with the goal of beginning volume production in the second half of 2027. CEO: agreement value will depend on material pricing, one-time or recurring licensing fees and royalties, and ultimately on customers' success with end users, typically hyperscalers and AI networking companies; no dollar value per agreement was given.
quarterly_data.figure: one supply and licensing agreement in place; volume production goal second half of 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Production readiness: headcount rose 25% sequentially, mainly in manufacturing scale-up, test engineering and commercial development; the company invested in equipment and clean room expansion for Perkinamine manufacturing and quality control. CEO: the Perkinamine production expansion in Denver is progressing, with new staff trained and new equipment being commissioned to increase batch size and output, preparing for a potential production ramp beginning in 2027. Back-end-of-line polymer integration is done in-house in Colorado today; Lightwave is engaged with external partners to outsource it for high volume and is working with one lead customer to build a scalable back-end production line.
quarterly_data.figure: headcount +25% sequentially; potential production ramp beginning in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Performance roadmap and foundry constraints: a 2026 priority is extending platform performance at 200 gigabits per second, 400 gigabits per lane and beyond, across scale-up, scale-out and now scale-across. CEO: silicon photonics foundries remain under pressure from strong demand, process development for novel materials and catching up on capacity (new sites, the move to 300-millimeter wafers). He declined to call Perkinamine the only viable material for CPO in scale-up, scale-out and scale-across, saying 'competition is fierce'.
quarterly_data.figure: 200 gigabits per second, 400 gigabits per lane and beyond
